page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% of evaluated hardware. Multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores fall within the average range, including software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing workloads. Memory bandwidth is moderate, registering 508.47 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 61.75 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark memory tests, which rank in the bottom 25%, highlighting a potential bottleneck for memory-intensive parallel operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-8 offers a dedicated hardware profile tailored for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints. The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a practical choice for workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 7.56 GB/sec, and Redis key-value operations, processing 7.98 million SET operations per second. It is also suitable for lightweight machine learning tasks, demonstrating average performance in small-model LLM inference, as well as general-purpose compute tasks like software compilation and image processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 4 physical cores. This instance provides a dedicated CPU allocation with a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, omitting local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance, while multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and software compilation fall in the average tier. Conversely, multi-threaded decompression and memory-intensive benchmarks show weaker relative performance. The qualitative cost profile favors compute-dense workloads over memory-heavy operations. It is best suited for static web serving, Redis database operations, software compilation, and lightweight CPU-based inference tasks.
